questions.prompt: The model ŷ = 2.2x + 0.8 is fitted to the data (1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 8), (4, 9), (5, 12). Find the residual for each point.

questions.grading_note: Form required: all five, in order. Residual = actual - predicted; the predictions are 3, 5.2, 7.4, 9.6, 11.8.

questions.prompt: Make a residual plot for the residuals 0, -0.2, 0.6, -0.6, 0.2 at x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
questions.prompt_markup: Make a residual plot for the residuals 0, -0.2, 0.6, -0.6, 0.2 at x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
questions.correct_answer: The points (1, 0), (2, -0.2), (3, 0.6), (4, -0.6), and (5, 0.2), scattered above and below 0 with no pattern
questions.grading_note: Any correct plot. The lack of a pattern supports a linear form; the small size of the residuals (all within 0.6) shows the errors are small.

questions.domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic & Exponential Models
questions.skill: Use logarithms to solve exponential models fitted to data
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A model fitted to bacteria counts is N = 150(1.4)^t, with t in hours. When does N reach 1,000? Give the exact expression and the value to the nearest tenth of an hour. (log means base 10.)
questions.prompt_markup: A model fitted to bacteria counts is N = 150(1.4)^t, with t in hours. When does N reach 1,000? Give the exact expression and the value to the nearest tenth of an hour. (log means base 10.)
questions.grading_note: Form required: the exact expression (any equivalent, such as log(20/3) ÷ log 1.4) and the rounded value. 1.4^t = 6.67, t ≈ 5.64.

questions.prompt: A line fitted to the logarithms of data is log y = 0.3x + 1 (log means base 10). Write y as an exponential function of x.
questions.prompt_markup:
A line fitted to the logarithms of data is log y = 0.3x + 1 (log means base 10).

questions.grading_note: Any equivalent exact form, such as 10^(0.3x+1) or 10(10^0.3)^x. A rounded base such as 10(2)^x is not exact: 10^0.3 ≈ 1.995.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Evaluate reports that use fitted models
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A report fits a line to the heights of children aged 5 to 15 and uses it to predict the height of a 40-year-old. What is the problem?
questions.prompt_markup:
A report fits a line to the heights of children aged 5 to 15 and uses it to predict the height of a 40-year-old.
What is the problem?
questions.correct_answer: It extrapolates far beyond the data; people stop growing, so the linear pattern does not continue.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Evaluate reports that use fitted models
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A report finds a strong correlation between ice cream sales and drownings and concludes that ice cream causes drowning. Do these observational data establish that conclusion? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
A report finds a strong correlation between ice cream sales and drownings and concludes that ice cream causes drowning.
Do these observational data establish that conclusion? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: No. A correlation in observational data does not establish causation; a lurking variable, such as hot weather, could increase both.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation that association alone does not establish causation. Naming a possible lurking variable is accepted but not required.
